title: Data Processing Readme
text:
This paper presents a new interpretation of the experimental data obtained by Roman Kisler for his PhD. All Roman’s data are kept here:-> smb://engpnns001.ad.unsw.edu.au/Fluid Mechanics Research/DAVIS_SHARED/My Projects/UNSW/AWT/Roman
A subset of Roman’s data is used for this paper. An explanation of how the data was processed is below.
There are two folders at the top:->
LeadingEdge:-> USP: main data extraction codes Roman_Hotwire: hot wire data processing Roman_Mean_Pressure: surface mean pressure processing
Plotting_Matlab:-> Contains the codes that process the data further as per the methods in the paper and produces most of trhe figures in theg paper. Full descriptions are below.

All codes are run in matlab.
run NEW_main__calib_and_analyse_USP.m

This reads experimental data taken by Roman Kisler for his PhD.
This reads the raw data and calibration data and produces two very big files:
This one creates the pressure jump spectra data: USP_savefile = “G_dpdp_Grid”+grids(igrids)+“_2DAirfoil_ZPG_AoA”+aoas(iaoas)+“_U”+speeds(ispeeds)+“.mat”; save(USP_savefile, ‘freq’,‘Pxx_calibrated’, ‘C_xy_calibrated’,‘G_dpdp’,‘Coh_jump’, ‘Coh_SS’,‘Coh_PS’,‘Phase_xy’,‘coh_length_PS’,‘coh_length_SS’, ‘aoas’, ‘grids’, ‘speeds’,‘pressure_taps’,‘tap_no_SS’,‘tap_no’)
This one creates the RMS data:
RMS_savefile = “RMS_Grid”+grids(igrids)+“_2DAirfoil_ZPG_AoA”+aoas(iaoas)+“_U”+speeds(ispeeds)+“.mat”; save(RMS_savefile, ‘freq’, ‘p_rms_avg’, ‘Lp_rms_avg’, ‘LPJ_rms_avg’,‘unit_G_pp’, ‘aoas’, ‘grids’, ‘speeds’,‘pressure_taps’,‘tap_no_SS’)

To obtain the surface Cp data, run:-> Panel_vs_exp.m

This will read the experimental data and create an eps file comparing a panel method calculation with the measurement (Figure 2 of paper).

The hot wire data presented in Fig 4 is created be running:-> Roman_HW_plot.m
Figure 5: rms of each tap vs x/c:-> RMS_plot_USPx_c.m
Figure 6: pressure jump rms vs x/c:-> RMSGDP_plot_USPx_c.m
Figure 7: experimental pressure jump psd:-> Gdpdp_plot.m
Figures 8 and 9: experimental pressure jump psd compared with Amiet theory:->Gdpdp_AMIET_plot.m
Figures 10 and 11: framework parameters:-> Frame_plot.m
Figure 12: phase jump measurements and model:-> PhasePJ_plot.m and pjump_model.m
Fig 13: phase across airfoil vs wavenumber with model:-> PhasePJ_plot.m
Fig 14: Experimental coherence and fitted model:-> COH_plot.m
Fig 15: Coherence parameters and models:-> plot_stats.m

title: Con Doolan’s Website
text:
Prof Con Doolan works in the School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering at UNSW Sydney.
He leads the Flow Noise group at UNSW and is an expert in aeroacoustics.

title: Short CV
text:
Professor Con Doolan has an honours degree in Mechanical Engineering and a PhD in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Queensland. After working at the University of Glasgow, Department of Defence (Australia) and University of Adelaide, he is now a Professor at the University of New South Wales, Sydney. Professor Doolan founded and leads the Flow Noise Group, a world leader in aeroacoustics, which concerns the measurement, prediction and control of noise produced by fluid flow.
Prof Doolan has held senior leadership roles, the most recent being Director of Postgraduate Research Examinations (Engineering) and Associate Dean (Education) for UNSW Engineering. I have recently completed the UNSW Senior Leaders Program (2025) and have been involved with external accreditation for national and international universities.
